caption_used: The performance of knowledge probing after editing with different editing methods on BioMedLM, where "Base" denotes LLM without editing. The x-axis shows co-occurrence number on a logarithmic scale, while the y-axis represents accuracy (ACC %). All six methods show improving accuracy with increasing co-occurrence frequency. ROME consistently achieves the highest accuracy, starting at approximately 51% and reaching roughly 66% at the highest co-occurrence numbers. MEND and MEMIT follow as the next best performers, with MEND reaching approximately 56% and MEMIT approximately 55%. Notably, IKE demonstrates a steeper improvement rate than FT, surpassing it at co-occurrence numbers above 10^2 to reach approximately 52% at the highest frequency. The Base model exhibits the lowest performance throughout, plateauing at approximately 44%.
raw_response:
The line plot compares the performance of six different methods (Base, FT, IKE, MEND, MEMIT, and ROME) by plotting "ACC (%)" against "Co-occurrence Number". The x-axis represents the co-occurrence number on a logarithmic scale, with tick labels at 0, 10^1, 10^2, and 10^3. The y-axis represents accuracy, labeled "ACC (%)", on a linear scale with tick marks every 5 units from 40 to 65. All six methods are represented by solid lines with distinct markers and colors, and all show an overall upward trend as the co-occurrence number increases across four plotted data points. The "Base" method, shown as a black line with circular markers, starts at approximately 38% at the lowest co-occurrence number and increases to level off around 44% at the highest co-occurrence number. The "FT" method (blue line, downward-pointing triangles) rises steadily from roughly 40% to 48%. The "IKE" method (red line, upward-pointing triangles) increases from about 43% to 49%. The "MEND" method (brown line, diamonds) grows from approximately 44% to 56%. The "MEMIT" method (purple line, hexagonal markers) increases from roughly 43.5% to 55%. Finally, the "ROME" method (green line, squares) records the highest values across all data points, starting at approximately 51% and rising to about 66% at the maximum co-occurrence number shown.
